hints: Which cells lie on each diagonal? Try writing down the row and column of every cell on both diagonals of a 3 × 3 grid and look for a rule.
One loop over the row index i is enough: the main diagonal cell is mat[i][i] and the other diagonal cell is mat[i][n−1−i]. When n is odd these two meet in the centre.

1. Let n = mat.length.
  2. For each i from 0 to n−1, add mat[i][i] and mat[i][n−1−i].
  3. If n is odd, subtract the centre mat[n/2][n/2] once.
  4. Return the sum.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Visit every cell and add it if i == j or i + j == n − 1.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Loop once over the rows and pick the two diagonal cells of each row directly, then remove the double-counted centre when n is odd.

explain: For the 3 × 3 sample, row 0 gives 1 + 3, row 1 gives 5 + 5, row 2 gives 7 + 9, total 30. n is odd, so the centre 5 was added twice; subtracting it once gives 25, which is returned. Each row contributes exactly two cells, so one pass is enough. Watch n = 1: the single cell is added twice and then subtracted once, which correctly leaves it counted once.
recognize: "Sum of the diagonals of a square grid" → index pattern [i][i] and [i][n−1−i], no nested loop needed.
javascript: function diagonalSum(mat) { const n = mat.length; let s = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { s += mat[i][i]; if (i !== n - 1 - i) s += mat[i][n - 1 - i]; } return s; }
